specimen: the West-gate of Moria (the Doors of Durin)

asset.what: the Doors of Durin, the West-gate of Moria, as Tolkien drew them
asset.why_not: the artwork ruling: the archive publishes its own measurement of a plate and not the plate. Supplied by the owner 11 August 2026 for measurement.

bands.what: the tengwar inscription running round the arch, in the mode of Beleriand
the crown and seven stars of Durin, the hammer and anvil, the star of Feanor, the two trees and the pillars
Tolkien's own hand-lettered English caption naming the mode and romanising the text

attested.where: Appendix E and Tolkien's caption on this plate

refused.what: the Mode of Beleriand's letter values
refused.why: binding the arch's tengwar to Sindarin phonemes needs each glyph segmented and ordered along a curved baseline, then aligned against the romanisation. That is an instrument, not a reading, and it does not exist yet.
refused.what_would_answer: connected-component segmentation of the arch band, ordered along the arch's fitted curve, aligned against the attested Sindarin. The alignment is SELF-CHECKING: a wrong segmentation gives a length mismatch against a text the corpus already holds.
refused.why_it_is_now_possible: the plate exists in the workshop. Before 11 August it did not, and the refusal rested on having no material at all.

ruling: The owner ruled 11 August 2026 -- 'yes, measure the West-gate inscription -- my request rules' -- and supplied the plate when the archive turned out to hold none. This publishes the MEASUREMENT. The plate itself is not republished, under the artwork ruling as amended 1 August.
note: Tolkien's own caption on this plate names the mode of Beleriand and gives the Sindarin in Latin letters, which makes it a bilingual key -- the only one the archive has for a mode Appendix E describes and never tabulates. The letter values are NOT derived here; `refused` says what would derive them.
